**1 — Scene:** Roast chicken with herb-coated baby potatoes. The vegetables on the separate side plate and the drink are excluded.

**2 — Vessel:** A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across. Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Roast chicken, including skin; baby potatoes with herbs; a light visible coating of oil on the potatoes. No substantial sauce is visible.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area covered | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density → weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| Roast chicken, edible meat and skin | 32% | 170 cm² × 1.05 cm = 179 ml | 0.95 → **170 g** | 215 | 366 kcal |
| Baby potatoes with herbs | 23% | 122 cm² × 1.8 cm = 220 ml | 0.9 → **198 g** | 85 | 168 kcal |
| Oil coating | Overlaps potatoes | Thin coating, approximately 4 ml | 1.0 → **4 g** | 884 | 35 kcal |

Food covers approximately **55% of the plate**, leaving the rim and some gaps exposed. The oil overlaps the potatoes rather than adding separate coverage.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **372 g of edible food and 569 kcal** is plausible for the visible chicken portion and roughly five baby potatoes. Chicken bones are excluded from the edible-weight estimate; their size and the amount of oil are the main uncertainties.
